questions.question: Define the arms race and describe its main stages from 1949 to the 1980s.
questions.expected_answer: An arms race is a competition between countries to build more and better weapons. The US monopoly ended when the USSR tested an atomic bomb (29 August 1949). The US tested a hydrogen device (Ivy Mike, 1 November 1952, about 10,4 megatons, roughly 700 times Hiroshima); the USSR followed in 1953 and tested the 50-megaton Tsar Bomba (1961). Delivery moved from bombers (B-52) to ICBMs (Soviet R-7, 1957) and submarine missiles (Polaris, 1960): the triad. MIRVs multiplied warheads; Reagan's SDI (1983). Stockpiles peaked at about 70 000 around 1986.

questions.question: Explain the theory of deterrence and the effects and costs of the arms race.
questions.expected_answer: Deterrence: having enough weapons to retaliate even after a first strike discourages attack, producing MAD; fear that the other side might gain a first-strike advantage kept both building (security dilemma, missile gap, military-industrial complex). Effects: duck and cover drills, fallout shelters, fear; atmospheric fallout (strontium-90 in teeth), harm near test sites (Marshall Islands, Semipalatinsk). Costs: trillions of dollars; large Soviet military burden contributed to collapse; money diverted from development; protest movements (CND 1958; New York march 1982).

questions.question: Describe the Cuban Missile Crisis and explain how it led to arms control.
questions.expected_answer: After Castro's revolution and the failed Bay of Pigs invasion (1961), Khrushchev placed missiles in Cuba. A U-2 photographed them (14 October 1962); Kennedy announced a naval quarantine (22 October); 27 October was the most dangerous day; on 28 October Khrushchev agreed to remove them for a US no-invasion pledge and secret removal of US missiles from Turkey. Arms control followed: the hotline and Partial Test Ban Treaty (1963), NPT (1968), SALT I and ABM (1972), INF Treaty (Reagan and Gorbachev, 1987) and START (1991); stockpiles fell to about 12 000.
